item.title: Sāriputta, if a bhikkhu, on reflection, knows: 'On the path I entered the village for alms, at the place where I walked for alms, and…
item.description:
Sāriputta, if a bhikkhu, on reflection, knows: 'On the path I entered the village for alms, at the place where I walked for alms, and on the path returning from the village, regarding forms cognizable by the eye, desire, greed, hatred, delusion, or ill-will have arisen in me' — then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome states. But if, Sāriputta, on reflection, a bhikkhu knows: 'On the path I entered... returning from alms, regarding forms cognizable by the eye, no desire, greed, hatred, delusion, or ill-will have arisen in me' — then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu should abide with joy and gladness, training day and night in wholesome states.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 151 – Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisutta

item.title: ( Calā ): Having been born, one must die, Having been born, one sees suffering, Fetters bind and harm, Therefore I do not delight in…
item.description:
( Calā ):
Having been born, one must die,
Having been born, one sees suffering,
Fetters bind and harm,
Therefore I do not delight in birth.
The Buddha teaches the Dhamma,
Leading beyond rebirth,
Destroying all suffering,
Helping me abide in truth.
Beings inclined to the form realm,
They are deluded by the formless realm,
If they do not know cessation,
They go to further rebirth.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.6

item.title: Furthermore, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of robe and praises contentment with any kind of robe. Venerable Sir, this is…
item.description:
Furthermore, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of robe and praises contentment with any kind of robe. Venerable Sir, this is the second quality I see in the Blessed One. Because of this quality, disciples honor, respect, revere, and make offerings to the Blessed One, and after honoring and respecting, they live depending on the Blessed One.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 77 – Mahāsakuludāyisutta

item.title: 'For a long time, Venerable Sir, I have known the Dhamma taught thus: "Knowledge comes to one who is concentrated, not to one who is…
item.description:
'For a long time, Venerable Sir, I have known the Dhamma taught thus: "Knowledge comes to one who is concentrated, not to one who is not concentrated." Venerable Sir, does concentration come first and then knowledge, or does knowledge come first and then concentration?' Then the Venerable Ānanda thought: 'The Blessed One has just recovered from an illness, not long after being ill. This Sakyan Mahānāma asks a very profound question. Let me take the Sakyan Mahānāma aside and teach him the Dhamma.' Then the Venerable Ānanda took the Sakyan Mahānāma by the hand, led him aside, and said to him: 'The virtue of a learner, Mahānāma, has been spoken of by the Blessed One. And the virtue of a non-learner has also been spoken of by the Blessed One. The concentration of a learner has been spoken of by the Blessed One. The concentration of a non-learner has also been spoken of by the Blessed One. The wisdom of a learner has been spoken of by the Blessed One. The wisdom of a non-learner has also been spoken of by the Blessed One. And what, Mahānāma, is the virtue of a learner?'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.73

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: 'Strong shall be our desire to undertake the higher training in virtue. Strong shall be our desire to…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: 'Strong shall be our desire to undertake the higher training in virtue. Strong shall be our desire to undertake the higher training in mind. Strong shall be our desire to undertake the higher training in wisdom.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.81

item.title: Master Gotama, I have doubt and uncertainty: 'How should one understand the Dhamma of Samaṇa Gotama?' - "Vaccha, enough of your doubt. Enough of your…
item.description:
Master Gotama, I have doubt and uncertainty: 'How should one understand the Dhamma of Samaṇa Gotama?' - "Vaccha, enough of your doubt. Enough of your uncertainty. It is because you doubt that uncertainty has arisen. I declare the coming-to-be, Vaccha, for one who has clinging, not for one without clinging. Just as, Vaccha, a fire burns when it has fuel, not without fuel. So too, Vaccha, I declare the coming-to-be for one who has clinging, not for one without clinging." - "Master Gotama, when a flame is blown far away by the wind, what does Master Gotama declare as its fuel?" - "Vaccha, when a flame is blown far away by the wind, I say that the wind itself is its fuel. At that time, Vaccha, the wind is the fuel (upādāna)." - "Master Gotama, when a being abandons this body and is reborn in another body, what does Master Gotama declare as the fuel for that body?" - "Vaccha, when a being abandons this body and is reborn in another body, Vaccha, I declare that at that time craving itself is the fuel (upādāna).

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 44.9

item.title: Leaving the forest, he runs to the forest, Freed from the forest, he runs back to the forest. Look at that person: Freed from bondage,…
item.description:
Leaving the forest, he runs to the forest,
Freed from the forest, he runs back to the forest.
Look at that person:
Freed from bondage,
He runs right back into bondage.

Iron, wood, or rope — these bonds,
The wise say, are not strong.
Longing for jewels and ornaments,
Longing for children and wives —
That is a much stronger bond.

The wise say that bond is strong.
It pulls one down, though loose, it is hard to free.
The wise cut it off,
And leave sensual pleasures, not looking back.

Those who are intoxicated with sensual pleasures
Throw themselves into the stream,
Like a spider into its own web.
The wise cut it off,
And leave all suffering, not looking back.

From: Dhammapada 334-359

item.title: You have no hut, You have no nest, You have no network, You are free from bonds. ( Blessed One ): I have no hut,…
item.description:
You have no hut,
You have no nest,
You have no network,
You are free from bonds.
( Blessed One ):
I have no hut,
I have no nest,
I have no network,
I am free from bonds.
( Devata ):
What do you call a hut?
What do you call a nest?
What do you call a network?
What do you call bonds?
( Blessed One ):
'Hut' is mother,
'Nest' is wife,
'Network' is children,
'Bonds' are craving.
( Devata ):
Good indeed, you have no hut!
Good indeed, you have no nest!
Good indeed, you have no network!
Good indeed, you are free from bonds!

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.19

item.title: Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the rainy season, in the autumn, when the crops are ripening, a cowherd, tending the cows, would strike…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the rainy season, in the autumn, when the crops are ripening, a cowherd, tending the cows, would strike the cows on this side and that with his stick, checking them and restraining them. Why is that? Because the cowherd sees that due to this he might incur death, imprisonment, beating, or blame. So too, bhikkhus, I saw the danger, the degradation, and the defilement of unwholesome states, and I saw the seclusion, the benefit, and the purification of wholesome states.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 19 – Dvedhāvitakkasutta

item.title: For them, the red-hot coals were extinguished, the smoke disappeared, the mortar and pestle fell askew. They ate in the evening for the evening meal,…
item.description:
For them, the red-hot coals were extinguished, the smoke disappeared, the mortar and pestle fell askew. They ate in the evening for the evening meal, in the morning for the morning meal. They went into villages, towns, and capital cities for alms. Having obtained food, they returned to their leaf huts in the forest to practice meditation. Vāseṭṭha, they 'jhāyanti' (meditated), meaning they reflected. 'Jhāyaka' was the second name that arose.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 27 – Aggaññasutta
